Best environment prevailing to go to Italy through the legal process: Expert
item.description:
Giuseppe Di Giovanni, Migration Expert, Embassy of Italy, explicitly expressed his opinion and said that presently the best environment is prevailing to go to Italy on an employment visa through the legal process.

He made the disclosure at a national consultation on 'Skills, Migration and Mobility: The Way Forward for Bangladesh,' organised by the Ovibashi Karmi Unnayan Programme (OKUP) was held on 28 September 2026 at Hotel InterContinental, Dhaka, says a press release.

The consultation was part of OKUP’s engagement in the Global Strategy for Skills Migration and Development (GS4S), a Horizon Europe project led by Radboud University and funded by the European Union.

Very high-profile migration experts presented their thoughtful deliberations on the occasion.

Giuseppe Di Giovanni, therefore, pointed out why are the potential youth from Bangladesh highly exploited by traffickers to go to Italy in such risky and vulnerable illegal ways, spending Tk 2-3 million.

He disclosed with delight that Italy is going to recruit 1,50,000 skilled workers by next year, and Bangladesh is on the list of countries of origin.

He reiterated that the visa fee for Italy is only 65 Euro, but the migration cost is exorbitantly high in Bangladesh.

Giuseppe Di Giovanni expressed his concerns about the undocumented migrants in Italy and mentioned that asylum seekers are abusing our legal process of migration.

He urged all the concerned ministries, departments, and aspirant potential migrants to avail the opportunity of the Talent Partnership Programme, which has been launched through a contract with Bangladesh in 2023. Through this programme, more skilled professionals can get employment in European Countries.

Among others, Prof. Tesseltje de Lange, Professor of Migration Law and Director of the Centre for Migration Law at Radboud University, Netherlands, and Elisa Fornalé, Principal Investigator at the University of Bern, joined the consultation as distinguished panelists and delivered lectures.

The consultations suggested adopting policies to promote legal migration in Europe through strengthening Bangladesh’s approach to skills, migration, and mobility.

Laira Cartanya Llach, First Secretary, EU Delegation to Bangladesh, also called for action on the prospect of the Talent Partnership Programme.

Another panelist in the consultations, Md Nurul Islam, former director of the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET) emphasised strengthening the skills training ecosystem of Bangladesh to overcome the challenges to synchronise that with the demand of Europe.

item.title: No political leniency over land grabs, vandalism, govt not involved in Zaima’s appointment
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson and Adviser Mahdi Amin said no political leniency is being given regardless of who the offender is.

Replying to a query from journalists about several recent incidents of land grabs, attacks and vandalism, Mahdi Amin highlighted the government’s position, saying that the Ministry of Home Affairs was working on the matters and had information about them.

The government wants to ensure a fair legal process, and the home minister has also made it clear that no political leniency is being given regardless of who the offender is, he added.

Mahdi Amin made these remarks at a press conference while replying to a query about the incidents that had taken place in different places over the past few days.

The press conference was held at Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Office on Wednesday afternoon to brief the media on Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, his meetings with world leaders and his overall visit to New York.

Mahdi Amin said 13 people had already been arrested over the attempted occupation of Chand Udyan. Eleven people had been arrested over the attempted land grabbing at Shyamoli Housing in Adabor. Thirteen people had been arrested over the attack on and damage to property at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur. Besides, seven people had been arrested over the vandalism of a content creator’s studio at ECB Chattar.

The government was working impartially and was taking legal action with the utmost sincerity wherever there was any wrongdoing or unlawful attempt, he added.

Mahdi Amin said maintaining stability in the law and order situation was the government’s top priority. If any miscreant attempts to create instability, it will be dealt with firmly, he said.

On Zaima Rahman

Zaima Rahman has been appointed as a legal officer at the office of Khalilur Rahman, president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Asked about the appointment, Mahdi Amin said the Bangladesh government had no connection whatsoever with the appointment.

Zaima Rahman was appointed directly through the UN Human Resources Department as a P-3-level legal officer. The Bangladesh government had no involvement whatsoever in the appointment process.

Mahdi Amin further said the UN Executive Office and Human Resources Department make appointments by following their own rules, regulations and procedures.

Anyone can visit the UN website to see the matter, he said.

According to the UN job classification, P-1 positions are for new graduates, P-2 positions require two years of experience and P-3 positions require at least five years of professional experience. As Zaima Rahman’s academic and professional profile matched the position, she was appointed on the basis of her qualifications and merit. There was no question of government funding or recommendation, he said.

Mahdi Amin added that, unlike the past practice of using political influence to secure positions at the UN or become part of delegations, Zaima Rahman had not done so; rather, she was working on the basis of her personal and professional skills.

At the press conference, questions were also asked about allegations that gas cylinders were being sold for Tk 200 to Tk 400 more than the fixed price.

Mahdi Amin said the matter would be brought to the attention of the relevant official. Gas, fuel and electricity prices have increased in various parts of the world due to the crisis in the Middle East. Despite this, the government has tried to keep fuel prices under control as much as possible to reduce pressure on ordinary people. If steps need to be strengthened to further regulate the market, the government will continue to take effective measures, he added.

Prime Minister’s Adviser Mahdi Amin described the prime minister’s participation in this year’s UN General Assembly as unprecedented. The prime minister gave a clear message about Bangladesh’s democratic uprising on the world stage. Bangladesh’s internal plans, programmes and policies for running the state, changing people’s fortunes, resolving problems and building a modern, people-oriented and humane state were presented. At the same time, Bangladesh’s position on world peace as a democratic and peace-loving country was also highlighted.

Mahdi Amin said that during the prime minister’s visit, besides the main UN General Assembly session, discussions were held with world leaders at around 11 bilateral meetings and various events. He said Bangladesh received a positive response internationally in these discussions.

Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Saleh Shibli and Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon were present at the press conference.

item.title: Compromise petition filed between Gazi Nazrul and Mariam’s family, PP says court didn't accept it
item.description:
A compromise petition between Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and the family of Mariam Akter, his second wife who died by suicide, was submitted to the court.

However, the court did not accept it, said public prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi.

Today, Wednesday, a bail hearing for Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Islam, was held before Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah.

The court granted bail only to Maksuda, considering her age and the fact that she is a woman.

Public prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi told Prothom Alo that the complainant, Md Masum Billah, Mariam’s father, told the court today that he had no objection if Gazi Nazrul and his first wife Maksuda Islam were granted bail.

The defence submitted a compromise petition along with the bail bonds, but the court did not accept it. The court granted bail to Maksuda Islam considering her age and gender, but rejected Gazi Nazrul’s bail petition.

“Had the court accepted the compromise petition, it would have granted bail to both of them. This case is not compoundable,” he said.

Defence lawyer Mahbubur Rahman, however, said the court had partially accepted the compromise petition.

He said the court accepted it in part and granted bail to Maksuda Islam, while rejecting Gazi Nazrul’s bail petition.

Asked whether this could be described as partial acceptance of the compromise petition, the lawyer said, “It can be.”

On the evening of 20 September, police recovered the hanging body of Mariam, Gazi Nazrul Islam’s second wife, from a flat at the NAM Bhaban opposite the Parliament complex. That night, police took Gazi Nazrul Islam and his first wife, Maksuda Islam, into custody. Later that night, Mariam’s father, SM Masum Billah, filed a case accusing Gazi Nazrul Islam, Maksuda Islam and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman of abetting suicide.

The following day, a court granted Gazi Nazrul Islam four days’ remand and Maksuda Begum one day’s remand following a petition by Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police Sub-Inspector Md Shamsujjoha Sarker. That night, the investigation of the case was handed over to the Detective Branch of police. After the remand, Maksuda Begum was sent to jail on 22 September. Nazrul Islam was taken on remand for eight days in two phases, four days each.

The third accused in the case, Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman, was arrested outside Dhaka by SRB-2. He was subsequently sent to jail through a court order.

item.title: BNP steps up action against controversial leaders, activists
item.description:
The BNP is taking a tougher stance against individuals accused of extortion, land grabbing, vandalism, violence and other criminal activities using the party’s name.
Following allegations against leaders and activists of the BNP and its affiliated organizations in different parts of the country, the party’s top leadership has stepped up efforts to identify controversial figures and take organizational action against those found responsible.
Party sources said allegations will be investigated and those found guilty will face necessary organizational measures, including expulsion, regardless of their position or influence within the party. In serious cases, the BNP will also cooperate with law enforcement agencies in taking legal action.
Senior BNP leaders said no one would be allowed to use the ruling party’s identity to pursue personal interests. At the same time, allegations made against the party for political purposes would also be scrutinized.
The party’s high command wants to follow a two-pronged approach—taking action against those proven to have committed offenses while politically countering allegations found to be false or motivated.
According to party sources, the activities of BNP leaders and activists as well as those of its affiliated organizations, including Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal, are being closely monitored.
Particular attention is being given to individuals who have repeatedly faced allegations of extortion, land grabbing, violence, vandalism or breaches of party discipline. Information about such allegations is being collected from the grassroots, and the party is preparing to take organizational decisions after verifying the facts.
BNP Vice Chairman Shamsuzzaman Dudu said there had been widespread discussion over allegations of extortion, toll collection and land grabbing, but many of those allegations were politically motivated.
“However, if any BNP leader or activist is proven to be involved in such activities, strict action will be taken,” he said.
Dudu said the party’s high command was monitoring the overall situation and examining the allegations. The same policy would be applied to anyone involved in activities that damage the party’s image, he added.
BNP Joint Secretary General Syed Imran Saleh Prince said the party would take action against anyone proven to be involved in criminal activities following proper investigations.
“No one can use the party’s name to serve personal or political interests,” he said, adding that law enforcement agencies should take strong action against extortionists and land grabbers.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has also spoken of a “zero-tolerance” policy against terrorism and criminal activities carried out in the party’s name.
Speaking to journalists, Rizvi said no one would be given any concession if they used the party’s identity to engage in unethical, illegal, violent or criminal activities.
He said organizational action had already been taken against several thousand BNP leaders and activists and those of its affiliated organizations in different incidents.
BNP leaders, however, stressed that merely being accused would not make someone a criminal. The circumstances of each incident and the individual’s actual involvement would have to be verified before any organizational decision was taken.
Through this approach, the party’s high command wants to counter allegations made against the BNP for political purposes while ensuring that genuine offenders cannot hide behind the party’s identity.
Names of individuals allegedly linked to local BNP units have surfaced in connection with attacks and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur and at the studio of content creator Salman Muqtadir in the ECB area. Investigations into the incidents are underway, and several people have already been arrested.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said no one would be spared if any political connection was established in the Radda health center incident.
Responding to journalists at the Secretariat on Wednesday, he said police operations against extortionists, criminals, arms carriers and drug dealers were ongoing and would be intensified.
He also said preparing lists of criminals was a regular responsibility of the police and that such lists were updated regularly.
“An offender will be treated as an offender. No political identity will be taken into consideration,” the home minister said, adding that having a political affiliation would not prevent legal action.
Salahuddin also said action would be taken against the police officer concerned over allegations of negligence of duty in connection with the Radda health center incident.
Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman said the government was concerned and embarrassed whenever citizens’ rights were violated, public or private establishments were vandalized, or people came under attack.
He said anyone found to be involved in such incidents through investigation would be brought under the law.
Meanwhile, a section of BNP grassroots activists has also demanded a cleansing drive within the party.
They argue that the activities of those who have been involved in the party’s long-standing political movements should not be equated with those who have recently sought to exploit the BNP’s name for personal benefit.
They have called for the prompt identification of individuals involved in criminal activities using the party’s name and demanded both organizational and legal action against them.
Grassroots BNP leaders also believe the party needs to remain vigilant about individuals presenting themselves as “hybrid” or “new BNP” members to prevent them from gaining influence by exploiting the party’s identity after it came to power.
They have also emphasized the need to assess an individual’s political background, organizational involvement and engagement with the public before assigning them positions in party committees.
The BNP’s central leadership also believes that strengthening organizational discipline is essential to preserving the political foundation built through years of movements and struggles.
Particular emphasis is being placed on establishing effective accountability mechanisms from the central level to the grassroots to prevent the misuse of the party’s identity while in power.
The party has already taken measures such as expulsion, withdrawal of organizational responsibilities and issuance of show-cause notices against BNP and affiliated organization leaders and activists in connection with various incidents.
There are also precedents for organizational action against individuals accused of violating party discipline or engaging in criminal activities using the party’s identity in Chilmari of Kurigram, Patgram of Lalmonirhat, Comilla and different parts of Dhaka.
BNP policymakers said the measures were not aimed at any particular individual or group but were intended to protect organizational discipline and the party’s image.
The central leadership’s key message, they said, was that no one should be allowed to benefit from political identity after committing crimes in the party’s name.
According to BNP policymakers, the party wants to demonstrate that political identity cannot be used as a shield against criminal activity.
At the same time, as the government has also said that the political identity of an offender will not be considered in taking legal action, the party’s disciplinary measures and enforcement of state law are moving towards a similarly firm position.
Asked about the issue, BNP Standing Committee member Nazrul Islam Khan said: “True activists of the nationalist ideology can never be involved in extortion or land grabbing. The BNP will not spare anyone who engages in criminal activities using the party’s name. Organizational action as well as legal action will be taken against them.”

item.title: DNCC administrator: Footpath eviction drive to continue, no compromise with obstructionists
item.description:
Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Administrator Md Safiqul Islam Khan on Wednesday said the ongoing drive to reclaim footpaths from illegal occupation will continue, with no compromise with those who obstruct the operation, in the interest of ensuring smooth movement for city residents.
“The eviction drive to clear footpaths will continue to ensure smooth movement for city residents. The drive to reclaim the footpaths will be carried out even if it means walking over my dead body to clear the way for the people,” he said.
The DNCC administrator made the remarks while inspecting the site of an attack on DNCC vehicles, police and journalists during an eviction drive in front of Hope Market at Mirpur-10 in the capital earlier in the day.
“Those who have created anarchy and attacked DNCC personnel, police and journalists during the eviction drive will not be spared,” he said.
Safiqul said DNCC has been conducting drives against illegal occupation and businesses operating on footpaths to ensure that city residents can walk freely.
He said Wednesday’s operation at Mirpur-10 was part of the ongoing drive and alleged that the attack was carried out at the instigation of people who had occupied the footpaths and their associates.
The attackers later fled after facing resistance from local residents, the administrator said.
He said DNCC and police will file separate cases against those involved in the attack and that those found involved will be arrested following investigation.
Safiqul also alleged that some people deliberately set fire to a mosque earlier in the day in an attempt to create disorder.
He said the government will not tolerate any conspiracy or attempt to create disorder in the interest of protecting public welfare.
The administrator thanked the residents of Mirpur for supporting the eviction operation, saying the day’s events showed that many residents want the footpaths to remain free of illegal occupation.
“If anyone again comes forward, at the instigation of others, to support illegal occupation of the footpaths, legal action will also be taken against them,” he said.
Safiqul urged residents to continue supporting DNCC’s eviction operations, saying they have been conducting the drives over the past several days in response to public demand.
“We are working according to the demands of the people, and it is our moral responsibility to do so. Therefore, our activities will continue out of a sense of responsibility. We seek your cooperation,” he said.
Referring to the corporation’s efforts to improve the environment around Mirpur-10, the administrator said an eviction drive was conducted two days ago beneath the footbridge at the Mirpur-10 roundabout.
Following the drive, trees were planted there to create a better environment and facilitate pedestrian movement, he said.
Safiqul said DNCC has adopted a similar plan for other areas under its jurisdiction to ensure free movement for residents.
He expressed his commitment to stand by DNCC officials who regularly conduct eviction drives to serve city residents.
Asked about street vendors, the administrator said DNCC previously held discussions and public meetings with hawkers and reached a decision that they would not sit on footpaths.
He said the city corporation issued 204 registration cards to hawkers to facilitate their temporary business at alternative locations.
“But after a few days, they did not keep their word. They insist that they have to sit here, but this is a passage for the people. They will not be allowed to sit here,” Safiqul said.
During the inspection, local political leaders and residents of Mirpur chanted slogans in support of the DNCC administrator and expressed support for the corporation’s efforts to keep footpaths free from illegal occupation.
They also assured DNCC of their cooperation in its efforts to reclaim the footpaths for pedestrians.

item.title: DU restores Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall name
item.description:
The name of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is being restored at the gate of a Dhaka University hall, replacing the name of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi.
The inscription “Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall” has been removed from the gate of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall, with “Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall” set to be restored.
Work to erase the existing nameplate began on Wednesday afternoon.
Dhaka University Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane said that the decision followed a resolution adopted at the university’s latest Senate meeting.
“Last time, the Senate decided to retain all the previous names. That is now being implemented,” he said.
The hall’s Senior Administrative Officer Md Jaban Ali said the administration was removing Hadi’s name in response to repeated requests from students.
“The students have been coming to us repeatedly and raising the issue verbally. Parents also become confused as students’ certificates carry one name while another name is being used for the hall. Now only ‘Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall’ will be written,” he said.
Asked whether the students had submitted a written application, Jaban Ali said there was no written application.
The hall’s previous nameplate was removed and replaced with “Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall” in December 2025 after Hadi was shot.
A banner bearing the new name had been put up at the hall’s main gate around 2:30am on December 19. At the time, hall union General Secretary Al Sabah said signatures had been collected from students and most of them supported the name change.
The Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) later demanded that the hall be renamed “Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall” and submitted a memorandum to the vice-chancellor.
Following the demand, the university Syndicate on January 8 recommended changing the hall’s name to “Shaheed Osman Hadi Hall”. It also recommended renaming Bangamata Sheikh Fazilatunnesa Mujib Hall as “Bir Pratik Captain Sitara Begum Hall”.
However, the June 29 Senate session did not reach a final decision on changing the names of five institutions named after members of the Sheikh family. Five Ducsu Senate members walked out of the session over the issue, after which the proposal was sent back to the Syndicate.
Meanwhile, the university’s official website continues to list the hall as “Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Hall”. The hall was established in 1988 and named after Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, according to the university’s website.

item.title: Trump says AI companies agree to ‘self-police’
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said a group of CEOs of Artificial Intelligence (AI) companies had signed an accord to “self-police” the technology’s development.
Trump met with AI leaders at the White House, where he doubled down on his support for the technology.
The agreement comes as public scrutiny has grown over the risks posed by the emerging technology, following reports that OpenAI and Anthropic’s AI agents had gone rogue and hacked into other companies’ systems.
Concerns are also mounting over the industry’s growing footprint in communities, particularly with the growth of data centers.
Prior to the meeting, Trump had reiterated that his government would not limit the development of AI or support calls for “guardrails” or other restrictions on the sector.
“I will never stifle the growth of a technology that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution,” Trump said. “We can’t stifle it, and we’re leading by a lot.”
Trump also announced that he would officially rename the technology “super intelligence” because “it’s not artificial.”
House Speaker Mike Johnson joined the meeting, which included top AI executives like Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI president Greg Brockman, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, and Elon Musk, whose X social media platform includes its own AI model, Grok.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also attended.
“I think I’m seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump told reporters during an impromptu press conference outside the West Wing.
Later, the US president posted a copy of the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence” on his Truth Social platform.
“Every company is responsible for developing its own technology safely and in a way that builds trust with customers and the public,” the accord begins.
The document affirms that tech companies will implement “robust internal controls to ensure all of the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended, and that any issues are remediated.”
They are to “empower an internal team” to ensure “control, monitoring, and detection” are working as intended.
AI companies are also expected to “partner with an independent external auditor or evaluator to carry out independent assessments,” as well as “designate an independent committee of the board of directors” to oversee and receive reports.
Trump said the agreement is “morally binding” but not legally enforceable.
The accord does, however, leave the door open “to codify these steps into laws or regulations.”

item.title: Ruman: Incidents orchestrated to divert attention from PM's US visit
item.description:
Prime Minister's Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Ruman on Wednesday said some incidents were orchestrated before and after Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's recent US visit to draw public and media attention away from his international engagements and achievements.
"Some incidents were brought to the fore just before the prime minister and his entourage left for the United States," he told a press conference at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister's Office in Tejgaon.
Ruman said, "When we were preparing to leave for America with the prime minister and his entourage, we saw that some incidents were made to happen. I will not say they happened; you will understand why I am saying this."
The same thing happened after the prime minister returned home following a successful visit, during which Tarique Rahman had a packed schedule of engagements from morning until late at night, he added.
Ruman said, "We expected that our success would be the subject of news coverage and discussions when we returned home. But then another incident took place, and I noticed that most of the media talk shows focused on that instead."
He said, "Those who are opposing us are perhaps still following the same formula through which the former government ran the country," he added.
Ruman said the incidents were first highlighted by some online media outlets and were later picked up by major online portals, newspapers and television channels, giving them wider public attention.
Using an analogy, Ruman said a government could not be expected to succeed if it was simultaneously being constrained. "If you let a person swim across a river but tie his hands and feet, will he be able to cross it? I will not be able to do it either," he said.
He urged the media to extend cooperation to the government, saying the Prime Minister wanted to build a "beautiful and civilized Bangladesh."
"We want your cooperation. We have repeatedly appealed to you to cooperate with us. Our prime minister, Tarique Rahman, truly wants to build a beautiful and civilized Bangladesh. Please cooperate with us," he said.
Prime Minister's Adviser Mahdi Amin, Prime Minister's Press Secretary AAM Saleh Shibly, Prime Minister's Speech Writer Mahfuzur Rahman, Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu, Deputy Press Secretary Md Suzauddhowla (Sujan Mahmud), Assistant Press Secretary Gazi Shahriar Pamir and Assistant Press Secretary KM Nazmul Haque Khan were present at the press conference.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s first wife secures bail in suicide abetment case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday granted bail to Maksuda Islam, the first wife of expelled Jamaat-e-Islami lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam, in a case filed over the abetment of the suicide of his second wife, Mariyam Akter.
The court granted Maksuda bail after Mariyam’s father and case complainant, SM Masum Billah, submitted a settlement deed and said he had no objection to her release.
However, the court rejected Gazi Nazrul Islam’s bail petition.
The matter came up during a bail hearing before Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah.
According to the settlement deed, notarised on Tuesday, Masum Billah said Mariyam did not die by suicide due to any provocation or actions by Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda, or out of anger or resentment towards them.
The deed states that Masum Billah initially filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman on suspicion that they had abetted her suicide.
It says he later learned through various sources that Mariyam had not taken her own life because of any provocation or actions by Gazi Nazrul or Maksuda.
Under the terms of the settlement, Masum Billah and his family will have no objection if Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda are granted bail in the case.
The deed also states that, after their release on bail, both sides will seek to maintain cordial family relations and cooperate as needed with the ongoing judicial proceedings.
The settlement concerns Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station Case No-16(9)26, filed under Section 306 of the Penal Code, 1860.
The deed was notarised by Notary Public ASM Hanif on Tuesday. Mariyam’s father, SM Masum Billah, signed it as the first party, while Md Abdul Hamid Morol signed as the second party.
Police recovered Mariyam’s hanging body from Flat 203 of NAM Bhaban in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar on September 20.
The door was locked from inside. With assistance from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), police broke open the door and recovered her body hanging from a ceiling fan. Several notes were also found in the room.
The following day, Masum Billah filed the case against Gazi Nazrul, Maksuda and Obaidur Rahman, accusing them of abetting Mariyam’s suicide.

item.title: Bangla QR to launch P2P transactions from November 1
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has announced that Person-to-Person (P2P) transactions via "Bangla QR" will officially launch on November 1 later this year.
This service will allow users to seamlessly transfer funds to another individual by scanning a Bangla QR code or uploading an image of a QR code through their respective mobile applications.
The announcement was made on Wednesday (September 30) during a press conference held at Bangladesh Bank headquarters, attended by central bank spokesperson and executive director Arief Hossain Khan alongside other senior officials.
To accelerate the adoption of Bangla QR, the central bank unveiled several key measures, including instant settlement of transaction funds to merchant accounts, reduction of payment processing fees, and financial incentives.
Currently, customers of banks and Mobile Financial Services (MFS) can scan Bangla QR codes across nearly 4 million merchants nationwide to pay for goods and services.
Bangla QR adoption has seen exponential growth in recent months.
In June, the platform recorded an average of 100,000 daily transactions totaling over Tk28 crore.
Currently, average daily transactions have climbed to nearly 350,000, valued at approximately Tk143.54 crore.
According to central bank data, within the 90-day window following July 1, the average daily transaction volume grew by 3.5 times, while the total transaction value surged nearly 5-fold.
Introduced by Bangladesh Bank as the nation’s unified, interoperable QR payment standard, Bangla QR aims to build a secure, simple, and inclusive digital payment ecosystem that extends financial access to marginal populations across all economic levels.
To consolidate QR payments, Bangladesh Bank mandated the replacement of all proprietary QR systems with Bangla QR starting July 1.
Starting October 1, funds processed through Bangla QR payments will be credited to the merchant’s account instantly.
The mandatory minimum 1% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for acquiring institutions has been abolished, and the interchange fee for issuing institutions has been set to zero.
This cost reduction allows banks and MFS providers to offer Bangla QR payment services to merchants either free of charge or at minimal rates.
For every Bangla QR transaction up to Tk2,000 processed through the National Payment Switch Bangladesh (NPSB), Bangladesh Bank will provide an incentive of 0.10% to acquiring institutions and 0.20% to issuing institutions.
To reinforce customer confidence, automated mechanisms have been established for rapid refunds on failed transactions.
Additionally, Bangladesh Bank issued guidelines on September 27 to ensure fast, transparent, and effective dispute resolution.
Customers with complaints or inquiries regarding Bangla QR transactions can contact the Bangladesh Bank hotline at 16236.

item.title: BCB decides to explore untapped cricket talents in hills
item.description:
Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has decided to explore untapped cricket talents in three southeastern hill districts (CHT) as the rugged terrain and lack of infrastructure visibly kept the sport beyond reach of many youngsters in the region, officials said.
“The board is mulling ways to onboard more players from ethnic minority communities into mainstream cricket system,” BCB director Sirajuddin Mohammad Alamgir said.
Alamgir, a strong advocate of the initiative, said the “biggest obstacle is not lack of their athletic ability but a lack of opportunity” and so the country's cricket structure must go beyond waiting for talented players from the hills to make their way on their own to established cricket centers.
“Instead, the system needs to take the game to them as it's not possible for them to overcome all hurdles to come to the city and play cricket,” he said.
BCB officials said their proposals include creating residential facilities in Chattogram, expanding training opportunities and providing financial support to promising players from remote areas of the Chattogram Hill Tracts (CHT) to enable them to develop their skills in a professional environment
Cricket experts said children in Rangamati, Bandarban and Khagrachhari hill districts often grow up in rugged terrain, geographic isolation having limited access to sports facilities while reaching a cricket ground often emerge as a major challenge for them.
Former BCB coach in Rangamati Mohitosh Dewan, himself a member of a minority ethnic community in the hills, knows that reality well.
“It's extremely tough to manage playing cricket in the hill tracts. When life is undeniably tough, cricket is a luxury there,” Dewan said.
He said young players often need to overcome significant logistical difficulties simply to reach a field and in most cases they firstly need to cross a chain of hills and waterlogged areas before reaching a cricket field.
Dewan said the geographic feature of the CHT made cricket fundamentally different from some other sports which gained popularity among ethnic communities. “The physical endurance developed by life in the hills has helped produce successful athletes in football, hockey and other disciplines, but cricket requires regular access to pitches, equipment, coaching and organized competition,” Dewan said.
Ethnic athletes have become prominent in several sports, with footballers such as Rituparna Chakma and Monika Chakma playing important roles in Bangladesh women's football while cricket, by contrast, so far produced only a handful of ethnic players in the country's organised system.
Champa Chakma became the first ethnic cricketer to represent Bangladesh women's cricket and later pursued a career as an umpire. Mohitosh Dewan played in the Dhaka Premier League in the 1990s before moving into coaching.
More recently, Anik Deb Barman and Leky Chakma have emerged through the BCB's age-group structure.
Their progress has given the BCB something which was missing for decades displaying visible examples that players from ethnic communities can enter the national cricket pathway if they are given the opportunity.
Anik, a 6-foot-3-inch Tripura fast bowler from Habiganj, has already reached Bangladesh's Under-19 preliminary setup. His route into cricket depicts the importance of access.
“We have 40 families in our community in the village. No one played cricket there and hardly have any interest in this sport,” Anik said.
He only received a serious opportunity after moving to Habiganj town, where a coach noticed him playing at school and helped pace his development.
Leky's journey was even more difficult as she had to overcome family resistance to her ambitions and travel several kilometres to attend training sessions.
Her breakthrough came through a district-level camp in Rangamati organized with the support of the local cricket association.
Champa, who was involved in the camp, immediately recognized her potential.
“There were 40 players in the camp. Leky showed her potential to be the next cricketer from the hill tracts. So I picked her and informed the management about her ability,” Champa said.
Leky subsequently went through rigorous training to make herself available for the Under-19 level.
Her progress is significant not only because of what it means for her career, but also because the BCB sees the possibility of creating a chain reaction -- one successful player could inspire many others to consider cricket.
Alamgir believes the absence of such a figure has been one of the reasons cricket has struggled to develop in the hills.
“You need a hero in our locality to embrace cricket. For hill tracts people, there is no hero,” he said.
He said a successful national-level player from an ethnic community could become a powerful source of inspiration for children who currently saw little connection between their communities and elite cricket.
But, he said, creating that role model will require more than identifying talented youngsters and the BCB must also address the economic realities as many children naturally gravitate towards sports that require less financial investment because of their circumstances in the hills.
“They are interested in less-costly games since they live under the poverty line. Daily realities of life in the hill tracts are very different from those in urban areas,” Alamgir said adding BCB now wanted to combine training with practical support for the region.
Alamgir proposed using existing facilities in Chattogram to establish a dormitory where promising young cricketers from remote communities could stay and train. He also wants the board to explore financial assistance.
“We can even give some a salary so that they can be motivated to play cricket. If we can prepare cricketers in this way from the hill tracts, there will be a revolution there,” he said.
The concept, however, is not entirely new as during his time at the Bangladesh Olympic Association, he proposed establishing a sports centre of excellence in the hill tracts, but the project never materialized.
BCB is now looks at a more targeted approach for cricket.
The board also recognises that physical strength alone cannot take a player to the top since cricket demands technical ability, tactical understanding and sustained coaching.
“T20 cricket is all about power” is a common perception but power alone is insufficient without the necessary skills. Intensive training is essential, Alamgir said.
That makes the development of ethnic cricket a long-term project rather than a short-term talent hunt.
BCB's challenge is to create a system through which children in remote communities can be identified early, given access to coaching and equipment, and then connected to the established age-group structure.
The emergence of Champa, Anik and Leky has demonstrated that the pathway is possible. The next step is to make it less dependent on individual circumstances and more accessible to an entire generation.
The hills have already produced athletes capable of competing at the highest levels in other sports, which cricket has lacked but BCB now wants to build that bridge.
For the board, the objective is clear -- find the talent, remove the barriers and give ethnic communities a genuine route into mainstream cricket.

item.title: India opposition parties call for protests over ‘vote theft’
item.description:
India’s opposition parties announced on Wednesday planned protests to “save democracy,” escalating their campaign against the election commission after a newspaper investigation suggested impropriety in a large-scale voter roll revision.
Politicians have accused the head of Election Commission of India -- long regarded as the guardian of the world’s largest democracy -- of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The election body has rejected the allegations, saying all its decisions were legally valid, while its chief Gyanesh Kumar has not commented.
“The main issue is the theft of votes,” said Rahul Gandhi, of the main opposition Congress party.
“We are going to ensure that those who have destroyed Indian democracy are punished,” he told reporters.
Opposition lawmakers will march to the Election Commission in New Delhi on Tuesday, and hold “save democracy” rallies countrywide in the days following, said Congress party chief Mallikarjun Kharge.
The Indian Express daily reported last week that some key decisions linked to the contentious revision exercise were likely taken without the approval of two of the three election commissioners.
The commission said the report gave “only one part of the picture.”
It maintains that the revision was intended to remove duplicate entries and prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from appearing on voter rolls.
Modi’s party has long alleged that undocumented migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently registered as voters. Many such migrants are Muslims.

item.title: Gaza health officials say Israeli strike kills 5 in Gaza City
item.description:
Gaza’s civil defense agency and a hospital said an Israeli airstrike targeting a minibus killed five people on Wednesday in a neighborhood southwest of the city.
Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesperson for the civil defense which operates as a rescue force under Hamas authority, told AFP there were “five martyrs and 20 wounded, including a number of children and women... as a result of an Israeli airstrike that targeted a passenger bus in Tel al-Hawa.”
Bassal said the bus was carrying civilians between Gaza City and the central and southern parts of the Palestinian territory.
He said it was hit “by two missiles fired by Israeli drones, which led to the destruction of its front and completely burned it.”
AFP has contacted the Israeli military for a response.
Gaza City’s Al-Shifa hospital confirmed that five bodies and several wounded people had arrived at the medical facility “following an Israeli airstrike that targeted a vehicle near the destroyed cabinet headquarters in the Tel al-Hawa neighborhood.”
The Gaza war was sparked by Hamas’s unprecedented 2023 attack against Israel, which resulted in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,000 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Israeli forces have killed more than 1,400 people since a ceasefire was announced last October, according to Gaza’s health ministry.
The Israeli military has identified five deaths in its ranks over the same period, as well as the death of one civilian contractor.

item.title: Iran says received US response to its proposal to end war
item.description:
Iranian authorities said on Wednesday they received the official US response to their proposal to end the Middle East war, state media reported, days after US President Donald Trump rejected the plan.
“At today’s cabinet meeting, the American side’s proposal was presented to President Masoud Pezeshkian by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi,” government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani told the official IRNA news agency, without specifying the content of the reply.
After seven months of conflict, indirect talks between the United States and Iran resumed last week on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Iran said it has put forward seven conditions for ending hostilities and reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for oil and gas exports.
The strait lies at the heart of the conflict between the United States and Iran, which began with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic in late February.
Tehran imposed a blockade on Hormuz after the war started, prompting Washington to respond with its own blockade on Iranian ports.
While not all conditions have been made public, Iran is notably demanding a ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah has been battling Israeli forces.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade.
Trump rejected the proposal when speaking to the press on Saturday, but Tehran had been awaiting an official response via Qatari mediators.
Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Tehran has continued to target ships in the strait.
Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country’s military, said on Wednesday that they have been striking small vessels that try to pass through the strait.
“We have been striking ships for quite some time now -- specifically the small vessels I mentioned that attempt to pass. We block their passage, yet the US has not retaliated for a while,” Guards spokesperson Hossein Mohebi told state TV.
The US, meanwhile, has stepped up its economic warfare against Iran, imposing sanctions on Iranian airlines and vowing to take a hard stance against foreign companies that provide them with assistance.

item.title: US-led coalition ends mission in Iraq
item.description:
A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight jihadists concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country’s leaders, but which some fear will embolden pro-Iran armed factions.
Coalition troops deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State group, which had seized large swathes of territory, committing massacres and forcing thousands of women and children into slavery.
The group was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group’s remnants.
The United States and Iraq agreed in 2024 to wind down the coalition’s mission, and its troops withdrew gradually from bases across the country, restricting their presence to the autonomous northern Kurdistan region.
On Wednesday, the US announced the mission’s formal conclusion.
“Today, the United States and our Coalition partners formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, consistent with the September 2024 US-Iraq joint statement and US national interests,” the Pentagon said.
The US Department of Defense however added that it would “continue to provide targeted training and intelligence support to our Iraqi partners.”
The US-led coalition did not defeat IS alone.
Kurdish Peshmerga fighters played an important role, as did powerful Iraqi factions, including pro-Iran groups that have yet to disarm.
The Iraqi government, which celebrated the withdrawal, believes it will deprive Iran-backed factions of the excuse they have used to retain their arsenal.
But many Iraqis fear the pullout might embolden the pro-Iran factions further and draw the country deeper into the Middle East war.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi hailed the end of the mission as the start of a new chapter.
“A new phase has begun, defined by Iraq’s sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, unity of decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends,” Zaidi said at a ceremony on Wednesday.
He had also declared that October 1 would be celebrated as Sovereignty Day.
It is “a national occasion that affirms the completion of Iraq’s path toward sovereignty and consolidates the presence of the state and its institutions,” the heads of Iraq’s executive, legislative and judicial branches said on Monday.
They added that “the presence of weapons outside state authority must be addressed... in line with timelines set by the government, in a manner that strengthens state sovereignty.”
Zaidi, who came to power this year with the US’s blessing, has vowed to reinforce the state’s monopoly on arms and ensure that armed factions hand over their weapons to the state.
His government initially set September 30 as the deadline for factions to disarm, but later withdrew the time limit as talks continued to “regulate” weapons -- an issue that has fueled division and is expected to take much longer to resolve.
Kurdish military commander Sirwan Barzani expressed disquiet over the withdrawal, saying: “We have no means to protect the skies of Kurdistan.”
He nonetheless told AFP that the Peshmerga forces remained prepared to confront any threats, stating that their “capabilities and experience have improved significantly thanks to the training, assistance and armament provided by the coalition.”
With several powerful groups refusing to disarm, senior politicians have intervened and are now hoping to work out a compromise deal.
Factions have put forward conditions that include not only the withdrawal of foreign troops, but also an end to American political and economic interference.
The powerful Kataeb Hezbollah group said the withdrawal of “the occupation forces... is a start towards achieving full sovereignty.”
But the group also threatened Zaidi’s government.
“A government that doesn’t work for the good of its people will be brought down by all possible means,” it said.
Pro-Iran groups have long demanded the withdrawal of US troops and began targeting them with drones and missiles, triggering US retaliatory strikes that killed several faction commanders over the years.
During the Middle East war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran and allied factions intensified their attacks in Iraq, targeting US-led troops in the Kurdistan region.

item.title: Golam Parwar: Government pushing country towards crisis over referendum
item.description:
Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar has said the government is pushing the country towards a crisis by discussing another referendum on constitutional amendments.
He also accused the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of misleading the people by ignoring the verdict of the February 12 referendum.
He made the remarks on Wednesday at a reception for meritorious students organized by Bangladesh Labor Welfare Federation at the National Press Club.
Golam Parwar said: “Not accepting the public verdict of the referendum is BNP’s first mistake. By talking about another referendum, the government is pushing the country towards a new crisis.”
He also questioned the government’s focus on the Constitution, saying the home minister was busy with the Constitution instead of carrying out the responsibilities of his ministry.
Golam Parwar also expressed concern over the country’s law-and-order situation.
He said: “Seeing the current situation, it seems there is no government in the country. People are beginning to lose confidence in the government due to the deterioration of the law-and-order situation.”
The program was presided over by Bangladesh Labor Welfare Federation President Advocate Atikur Rahman.
Associate Professor Hasan Ul Banna of Ibn Sina Medical College and central leader of Islami Chhatra Shibir Azizur Rahman Azad also spoke at the event.

item.title: Ahmad Al Safa, 12, nominated for Int’l Children’s Peace Prize 2026
item.description:
At just 12 years old, Bangladeshi child rights advocate Ahmad Al Safa has been nominated for the International Children’s Peace Prize 2026, placing his work for children’s rights, digital safety and gender equality on an international platform.
Nominated by Shafikul Islam, Ahmad is among the young changemakers being recognized in 2026 for taking action on issues that directly affect children and young people. His nomination highlights his work across three major themes: Climate Justice and Environment, Digital Safety, and Gender Equality.
Ahmad is also the younger brother of Bangladeshi youth activist and social entrepreneur Shahi Al Sadat, who has been involved in youth-led advocacy and child protection initiatives. Growing up in an environment closely connected to youth advocacy and social-impact work, Ahmad developed an early awareness of the challenges faced by children and young people.
Ahmad’s journey into child advocacy began when he was only 10 years old. Having grown up witnessing violence against children, harassment, cyberbullying, child marriage and other violations of children’s rights, he developed a strong sense of responsibility toward protecting and empowering children.
Rather than simply speaking about these challenges, Ahmad began working directly with children and communities. Over the years, he has participated in and supported awareness campaigns, educational programs and training initiatives across schools, communities and online platforms.
His advocacy addresses some of the most pressing challenges facing children today—including child marriage, violence against children, gender inequality, cyberbullying and online harassment. His work encourages young people to understand their rights, recognize potential threats and seek help when their safety is at risk.
Championing Digital Safety
Digital safety has emerged as one of the defining areas of Ahmad’s advocacy. Through awareness and training initiatives, he works to help children understand the risks of cyberbullying, online harassment and digital crimes while encouraging them to speak up and seek support.
At a time when children are increasingly exposed to risks in online spaces, Ahmad’s work focuses on equipping young people with the knowledge and confidence to navigate the digital world more safely.
According to his International Children’s Peace Prize nomination profile, Ahmad’s awareness and training initiatives have reached more than 20,000 children and families.
Despite being only 12, Ahmad continues to balance his education with social work, advocacy and community engagement. His nomination also recognizes the important role of his family in supporting his efforts and enabling him to continue his work at such a young age.
The International Children’s Peace Prize recognizes children and young people who have made significant contributions toward promoting children’s rights and creating a more peaceful and just world.
Ahmad Al Safa’s 2026 nomination brings international attention to a young Bangladeshi advocate working on issues that affect millions of children—particularly safety, equality, protection and digital rights.
For Bangladesh, his nomination represents a notable example of a young person stepping forward to address challenges faced by his own generation. At only 12, Ahmad’s journey demonstrates that meaningful advocacy can begin at a very young age—and that young voices can play an important role in shaping conversations around children’s rights and safety.

item.title: রাজ্যগুলোর কাছে নাগরিকদের ধর্মভিত্তিক তথ্য চেয়েছে ভারতের স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয়
item.description:
ভারতে জনসংখ্যা পর্যালোচনার জন্য গঠিত উচ্চপর্যায়ের কমিটি (হাই লেভেল কমিটি অন ডেমোগ্রাফিক চেঞ্জেস) বিভিন্ন নাগরিক তথ্যের ধর্মভিত্তিক হিসাব চেয়েছে।

এই নথিতে বিগত ১৫ বছরে প্রাথমিক ও মাধ্যমিক স্কুলে ছাত্র ভর্তি, গাড়ি কেনাবেচার হিসাব, জন্ম নথিভুক্তকরণ এবং জমি-সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তরের মতো ক্ষেত্রে ধর্মভিত্তিক তথ্য দিতে ভারতের রাজ্যগুলোকে বলা হয়েছে। যদিও এভাবে তথ্য দেওয়া প্রায় অসম্ভব বলে ইতিমধ্যেই জানিয়েছে ভারতের বিভিন্ন রাজ্য।

বিষয়টির তীব্র সমালোচনা করে কংগ্রেস নেতা জয়রাম রমেশ বলেছেন, এটি স্পষ্টই একটা ‘স্পষ্টত অত্যন্ত খারাপ উদ্দেশ্যমূলক কর্মসূচি’। সংবাদমাধ্যমের প্রতিবেদন উদ্ধৃত করে কেন্দ্রীয় সরকারের তীব্র সমালোচনা করে তিনি বলেন, এই কমিটির একটি স্পষ্ট ও পক্ষপাতদুষ্ট উদ্দেশ্য রয়েছে। দেখা যাবে, চূড়ান্ত রিপোর্ট হয়তো আগেই তৈরি করে রাখা হয়েছে।

২০২৬ সালের মে মাসে সাবেক বিচারপতি প্রকাশ প্রভাকর নাওলকরের নেতৃত্বে গঠিত এই কমিটি সম্প্রতি রাজ্য সরকারগুলোর কাছে ৩৫ দফার একটি বিস্তারিত প্রশ্নাবলি পাঠিয়েছে। এই নথিতে বিগত ১৫ বছরে প্রাথমিক ও মাধ্যমিক স্কুলে ছাত্র ভর্তি, গাড়ি কেনাবেচার হিসাব, জন্ম নথিভুক্তকরণ এবং জমি-সম্পত্তি হস্তান্তরের মতো ক্ষেত্রে ধর্মভিত্তিক তথ্য চাওয়া হয়েছে।

এর পাশাপাশি তফসিলি উপজাতি সম্প্রদায়ের মধ্যে ধর্মান্তরসংক্রান্ত গোয়েন্দা প্রতিবেদন, বিভিন্ন জেলায় অবস্থিত উপাসনালয় এবং আধার, ভোটার কার্ড বা রেশন কার্ড অস্বাভাবিক বৃদ্ধির বিবরণ চাওয়া হয়েছে। তফসিলি উপজাতিদের একটা বড় অংশ ভারতে খ্রিষ্টধর্মাবলম্বী।

ভারতের বিভিন্ন সংবাদমাধ্যমের প্রতিবেদন বলছে, রাজ্য প্রশাসনের কর্মকর্তারা জানিয়েছেন, সাধারণ প্রশাসনিক ব্যবস্থায় এ ধরনের নিত্যদিনের নাগরিক সেবার তথ্য ধর্ম পরিচয়ের ভিত্তিতে আলাদা করে রাখা হয় না। ফলে এত বিপুল ও জটিল তথ্য সরবরাহ করা রাজ্যগুলোর পক্ষে কার্যত অসম্ভব হয়ে দাঁড়িয়েছে।

কেন্দ্রীয় স্বরাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী অমিত শাহ ইতিমধ্যেই এই উচ্চপর্যায়ের কমিটির কাজ দ্রুত শেষ করতে গোয়েন্দা সংস্থা ও প্রশাসনিক কর্মকর্তাদের সার্বিক সহযোগিতার নির্দেশ দিয়েছেন। তবে বিরোধী শিবিরের মূল উদ্বেগ হলো, নিরপেক্ষ গবেষণার দোহাই দিয়ে সাধারণ নাগরিক পরিষেবা, শিক্ষা ও সম্পত্তির মতো মৌলিক বিষয়ে ধর্মভিত্তিক পরিসংখ্যান অনুসন্ধানের প্রক্রিয়াটি সমাজে বিভাজন তৈরি করবে। দীর্ঘ মেয়াদে এটি বিশেষ করে সীমান্তবর্তী অঞ্চলের প্রান্তিক মানুষদের অধিকারকে সংকুচিত করতে ব্যবহৃত হতে পারে বলে আশঙ্কা করা হচ্ছে।

কংগ্রেসের অভিযোগ

কংগ্রেসের মতে, জনসংখ্যার রূপান্তর পর্যালোচনার মোড়কে এই প্রক্রিয়া মূলত একটি বিশেষ সম্প্রদায়কে এবং বিশেষ করে সীমান্তবর্তী এলাকার সাধারণ মানুষকে বিভ্রান্ত ও হেনস্তা করার মানসিকতা থেকে পরিচালিত। কংগ্রেসের শীর্ষ পর্যায়ের নেতা জয়রাম রমেশ এই প্রক্রিয়াকে ‘পেটেন্টলি ডায়াবলিক্যাল এজেন্ডা’ বা ‘স্পষ্টত অত্যন্ত খারাপ উদ্দেশ্যমূলক কর্মসূচি’ বলে চিহ্নিত করেছেন।

কংগ্রেসের বক্তব্য, সীমান্ত জেলাগুলোতে ভোটারের সংখ্যা নিয়ে তদন্তের নির্দেশ দেওয়ায় গ্রামীণ ও প্রান্তিক জনগোষ্ঠী চরম অনিশ্চয়তায় পড়ছে। বিরোধীদের অভিযোগ, স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয় ও গোয়েন্দা বিভাগের প্রশাসনিক ও ডেটাসংক্রান্ত পূর্ণ সমর্থনের কারণে এই কমিটি সাধারণ পর্যালোচনার চেয়ে অনেক বেশি প্রশাসনিক চাপ সৃষ্টি করছে এবং সামাজিক মেরুকরণ ঘটাচ্ছে।

item.title: বাংলাদেশের প্রধানমন্ত্রীর ভারত সফর দুই দেশের মানুষই চায়: ভারতের হাইকমিশনার

item.title: টেলিটকের সেবার মান বাড়াতে ব্যবস্থা নেওয়ার সুপারিশ
item.description:
সরকারি মোবাইল সেবাদাতা কোম্পানি টেলিটকের সেবার মান বাড়াতে প্রয়োজনীয় উদ্যোগ নেওয়ার সুপারিশ করেছে ডাক, টেলিযোগাযোগ ও তথ্যপ্রযুক্তি মন্ত্রণালয়–সম্পর্কিত সংসদীয় স্থায়ী কমিটি। আজ বুধবার সংসদ ভবনে অনুষ্ঠিত কমিটির বৈঠকে এই সুপারিশ করা হয়।

চলতি সংসদে এই কমিটির প্রথম বৈঠক ছিল আজ। বৈঠক সূত্র জানায়, প্রথম বৈঠকে মূলত মন্ত্রণায়ের অধীন বিভিন্ন সংস্থা–প্রতিষ্ঠানের কার্যক্রম সম্পর্কে সংসদীয় কমিটিকে জানানো হয়। বৈঠকের কার্যপত্রে সংশ্লিষ্ট সংস্থাগুলোর বিভিন্ন কার্যক্রম ও ভবিষ্যৎ পরিকল্পনার কথা তুলে ধরা হয়। সেখানে টেলিটকের পক্ষ থেকে যে তথ্য দেওয়া হয়েছে, তাতে দেখা যায় গত পাঁচ অর্থবছরের কোনোটিতেই রাজস্ব লক্ষ্যমাত্রা পূরণ করতে পারেনি টেলিটক। সংস্থাটি আগামী পাঁচ বছরে তাদের অগ্রাধিকার ও উন্নয়ন পরিকল্পনার কথা তুলে ধরে।

টেলিটকের পরিকল্পনার মধ্যে রয়েছে, আগামী পাঁচ বছরের প্রান্তিক এলাকায় গ্রাহকসংখ্যা বাড়ানো; হাওর, পার্বত্য ও দ্বীপের মতো দুর্গম প্রান্তিক এলাকার বিদ্যমান কভারেজের ১০ শতাংশ বাড়ানো; শিক্ষাপ্রতিষ্ঠানে উচ্চগতির ইন্টারনেট সেবা বাড়ানো ইত্যাদি।

বৈঠক শেষে সংসদ সচিবালয়ের এক সংবাদ বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে জানানো হয়, কমিটি টেলিটকের সেবার মান বৃদ্ধির লক্ষ্যে প্রয়োজনীয় কার্যক্রম গ্রহণের সুপারিশ করেছে। এ ছাড়া নতুন প্রজন্মকে গড়ে তোলা এবং কর্মসংস্থান সৃষ্টির উদ্দেশ্যে তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তির বহুমুখী ব্যবহার নিশ্চিত করা ও জ্ঞানভিত্তিক সমাজ প্রতিষ্ঠায় সহায়তা দেওয়ার সুপারিশ করা হয়েছে।

বৈঠকে ডাক বিভাগের ডেটাবেজে সব নাগরিকের ঠিকানা সংরক্ষণ কার্যক্রম, ব্রডব্যান্ড অবকাঠামো সম্প্রসারণ, নির্ভরযোগ্য ও সাশ্রয়ী সেবা, এআই-সক্ষম বাংলাদেশ গঠন, ডিজিটাল পেমেন্ট প্রচলনে সহায়তা, কলসেন্টারের মাধ্যমে গ্রাহকের অভিযোগ নিষ্পত্তি, সাইবার সিকিউরিটি এবং দেশের শিশু–কিশোরসহ মাধ্যমিক পর্যায়ের শিক্ষার্থীদের জন্য নিরাপদ ইন্টারনেট ব্যবহার নিশ্চিতকরণ প্রকল্পগুলো আরও গতিশীল করার বিষয়ে গুরুত্ব দেওয়া হয়।

কমিটির সভাপতি কলিম উদ্দিন আহমেদের সভাপতিত্বে সদস্যদের মধ্যে বৈঠকে অংশ নেন ডাক, টেলিযোগাযোগ ও তথ্যপ্রযুক্তমন্ত্রী ফকির মাহবুব আনাম, আবুল খায়ের ভূঁইয়া, তমিজ উদ্দিন, মোবাশ্বের আলম ভূঁইয়া, মানসুরা আক্তার, কেরামত আলী এবং সাইদ উদ্দিন আহমাদ হানজালা।

item.title: ডেঙ্গুতে আরও ৬ মৃত্যু, হাসপাতালে ১,৯৪৮
item.description:
দেশে ডেঙ্গুতে আক্রান্ত হয়ে আরও ৬ জনের মৃত্যু হয়েছে। এডিস মশাবাহিত এ রোগ নিয়ে নতুন করে ১ হাজার ৯৪৮ জন বিভিন্ন হাসপাতালে ভর্তি হয়েছেন। এ নিয়ে চলতি বছর ডেঙ্গুতে ২৪৫ জনের মৃত্যু হলো। আর ডেঙ্গুতে আক্রান্ত হয়ে হাসপাতালে মোট ভর্তির সংখ্যা ৭৯ হাজার ৬২০।

আজ বুধবার স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তরের ডেঙ্গুবিষয়ক নিয়মিত প্রতিবেদনে এসব তথ্য জানানো হয়।

এতে বলা হয়, ডেঙ্গু নিয়ে মৃত্যু ও নতুন করে আক্রান্ত হওয়ার এসব ঘটনা ঘটেছে মঙ্গলবার সকাল আটটা থেকে আজ সকাল আটটা পর্যন্ত।

স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তরের তথ্য অনুযায়ী সর্বশেষ ২৪ ঘণ্টায় ডেঙ্গু নিয়ে সর্বোচ্চ ৩৪৩ জন ভর্তি হয়েছেন চট্টগ্রাম বিভাগের বিভিন্ন হাসপাতালে। দ্বিতীয় সর্বোচ্চ ৩২০ জন ঢাকা বিভাগের (ঢাকার দুই সিটির বাইরে) বিভিন্ন হাসপাতালে ভর্তি হয়েছেন। এ ছাড়া খুলনা বিভাগে ২৪৮ জন, বরিশালে ২১২, রাজশাহীতে ২১১, ঢাকা দক্ষিণ সিটিতে ২১০, ঢাকা উত্তর সিটিতে ১৮৯, ময়মনসিংহে ১০২, রংপুরে ৯৯ ও সিলেট বিভাগে ১৪ জন হাসপাতালে ভর্তি রয়েছেন।

সর্বশেষ ২৪ ঘণ্টায় ১ হাজার ৮৮২ ডেঙ্গু রোগী হাসপাতাল ছেড়েছেন বলে জানিয়েছে স্বাস্থ্য অধিদপ্তর। এ নিয়ে হাসপাতালে ভর্তির পর ৭৩ হাজার ৮৯০ ডেঙ্গু রোগী চিকিৎসা শেষে হাসপাতাল থেকে ছাড়পত্র পেলেন।

চলতি বছরের মে মাস থেকে দেশে ডেঙ্গুর সংক্রমণ বাড়তে শুরু করে। এরপর প্রতি মাসে রোগী বাড়তে থাকে প্রায় দ্বিগুণ হারে। সর্বশেষ গত আগস্ট মাসে ২০ হাজার ৫৩৬ রোগী ডেঙ্গু নিয়ে হাসপাতালে ভর্তি হন। ওই মাসে মারা যান ৪৩ জন। সেপ্টেম্বরে (গতকাল পর্যন্ত) ৪৩ হাজার ৭৭৪ জন ডেঙ্গুতে আক্রান্ত হয়েছেন। মারা গেছেন ১৪৮ জন।

item.title: আমিরাতের সঙ্গে তথ্য আদান-প্রদান ও আইনি সহায়তা জোরদারের আহ্বান আইনমন্ত্রীর
item.description:
বাংলাদেশ ও সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের মধ্যে তথ্য আদান-প্রদান এবং পারস্পরিক আইনি সহায়তা আরও জোরদারে গুরুত্বারোপ করেছেন আইন, বিচার ও সংসদ বিষয়কমন্ত্রী মো. আসাদুজ্জামান।
মঙ্গলবার (২৯ সেপ্টেম্বর) আবুধাবিতে অনুষ্ঠিত ১৫তম জাতিসংঘ অপরাধ প্রতিরোধ ও ফৌজদারি বিচার কংগ্রেসের সাইডলাইনে সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের বিচার মন্ত্রী আবদুল্লাহ বিন সুলতান বিন আওয়াদ আল নুয়াইমির সঙ্গে সাক্ষাৎকালে আইনমন্ত্রী এ গুরুত্বারোপ করেন।
আইন মন্ত্রণালয়ের এক সংবাদ বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে এ তথ্য জানানো হয়েছে।
বিজ্ঞপ্তিতে বলা হয়, আইনমন্ত্রী কংগ্রেস আয়োজনের জন্য সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের বিচারমন্ত্রীর প্রতি আন্তরিক কৃতজ্ঞতা প্রকাশ করেন। একই সঙ্গে সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতে বসবাসরত প্রায় ১২ লাখ বাংলাদেশি প্রবাসীকে আতিথেয়তা এবং দেশটির অর্থনৈতিক ও উন্নয়ন কর্মকাণ্ডে তাদের অবদানের সুযোগ করে দেওয়ার জন্য সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের প্রতি ধন্যবাদ জানান। এ সময় সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের বিচারমন্ত্রী দেশটির উন্নয়ন কর্মকাণ্ডে প্রবাসী বাংলাদেশিদের গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অবদানের জন্য তাদের প্রশংসা ও কৃতজ্ঞতা জানান।
এ ছাড়া আইনমন্ত্রী সফররত বাংলাদেশ প্রতিনিধিদলের প্রতি উষ্ণ আতিথেয়তা ও চমৎকার ব্যবস্থাপনার জন্য সংযুক্ত আরব আমিরাতের বিচারমন্ত্রীর প্রতি আন্তরিক ধন্যবাদ জানান।
এই সাক্ষাৎকালে আইন ও বিচার বিভাগের অতিরিক্ত সচিব মো. খাদেম উল কায়েস, আইনমন্ত্রীর একান্ত সচিব মো. সাজ্জাদুর রহমানসহ বাংলাদেশ প্রতিনিধি দলের অন্যান্য সদস্যরা উপস্থিত ছিলেন। বাসস।
